# I. Poisson Regression (Lecture 12)

**Poisson Log-Linear Model (canonical log link):**
$$\log\mu_i = \mathbf{x}_i^T\boldsymbol{\beta}, \quad \mu_i = \exp(\mathbf{x}_i^T\boldsymbol{\beta})$$

-   $\beta_j$: change in **log mean count** per unit of $x_j$.
-   $\exp(\beta_j)$: **rate ratio** (multiplicative effect on mean
    count).

**Goodness of Fit (**$\chi^2_{n-p}$ when $\mu_i$ large):

-   **Deviance:** $D=2\sum\{y_i\log(y_i/\hat\mu_i)-(y_i-\hat\mu_i)\}$
-   **Pearson** $\chi^2$: $G=X^2=\sum(y_i-\hat\mu_i)^2/\hat\mu_i$

**Poisson Rate & Offset:** When events occur over exposure $n_i$ at rate
$\lambda_i$:
$$E(Y_i)=\mu_i=n_i\lambda_i \;\Rightarrow\; \log\mu_i=\log n_i+\mathbf{x}_i^T\boldsymbol{\beta}$$

-   Offset is **fixed** (coefficient = 1, not estimated).

# II. Overdispersion (Lecture 13)

**Definition:** $\text{Var}(Y)>E(Y)$, i.e., $\text{Var}(Y)=\phi\mu$ with
$\phi>1$.

**Diagnostics:**

-   **Half-normal plot:** Order $|r_{(i)}|$, plot vs
    $\Phi^{-1}(\frac{n+i+0.5}{2n+1.125})$. Reference $y=x$. Slope
    $\approx\sqrt\phi$. Constant overdispersion $\Rightarrow$ linear
    deviation.

**Method 1: Quasi-Poisson (Dispersion Parameter):**
$$\hat\phi=\frac{G}{n-p}=\frac{1}{n-p}\sum\frac{(y_i-\hat\mu_i)^2}{\hat\mu_i}$$$$\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}_Q=\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}_{MLE},\quad\text{cov}(\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}_Q)=\hat\phi\cdot\text{cov}(\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}_{MLE})$$

**Deviance Analysis (F-test) with overdispersion** for nested
$M_0\subset M_1$ :
$$F=\frac{(D_0-D_1)/(p_1-p_0)}{\hat\phi}\sim F_{p_1-p_0,\,n-p_1},\;\hat\phi=G_{M_1}/(n-p_1)$$

**Method 2: Negative Binomial Regression:**
$$E(Y)=\mu,\quad\text{Var}(Y)=\mu+\mu^2/\phi$$

-   $\phi\to\infty\Rightarrow$ Poisson.

## Zero-Inflated Poisson (ZIP)

When data have **excessive zeros**:

-   Latent $Z_i$ (binary): $P(Z_i=0)=\pi_i$ (always zero).
-   $Y_i|Z_i=0\equiv0$; $Y_i|Z_i=1\sim\text{Poisson}(\lambda_i)$.
-   Model: $\log(\lambda_i)=\mathbf{x}_i\boldsymbol{\beta}$ and
    $\text{logit}(\pi_i)=\mathbf{z}_i\boldsymbol{\gamma}$
    (different/same predictors).
-   $P(Y=0)=\pi+(1-\pi)e^{-\lambda}$.

# III. LDA: Overview (Lectures 15-20)

**Three Modeling Approaches:**

-   **Marginal:** $E(Y_{ij})=\mathbf{X}_{ij}^T\boldsymbol{\beta}$,
    $\text{Var}(\mathbf{Y}_i)=\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_i$.
-   **Mixed effects:**
    $E(Y_{ij}|\boldsymbol{\beta}_i)=\mathbf{X}_{ij}^T\boldsymbol{\beta}_i$,
    $\boldsymbol{\beta}_i=\boldsymbol{\beta}+\mathbf{U}_i$.
-   **Transition:** $E(Y_{ij}|Y_{i,j-1},...,Y_{i1},\mathbf{X}_{ij})$.

## Covariance Pattern Models - GLS (Lecture 16)

**(a) Compound Symmetry / Exchangeable:** $\text{Var}=\sigma^2$,
$\text{corr}=\rho$ (any pair). 2 params. Strong assumption.

**(b) Toeplitz:** $\text{corr}(Y_{ij},Y_{i,j+k})=\rho_k$. $n$ params.
Equal time intervals only.

**(c) Autoregressive AR(1):** Special Toeplitz: $\rho_k=\rho^k$. **2
params** total. Equal intervals.

**(d) Banded:** corr=0 beyond an interval.

**(e) Exponential:** $\text{corr}(Y_{ij},Y_{ik})=\rho^{|t_j-t_k|}$.
AR(1) generalization for **uneven** times.

**(f) Unstructured:** All variances/covariances free. Most flexible,
most params.

## Linear Mixed Effects - LMM (Lecture 17)

**General LMM:**
$\mathbf{Y}_i=\mathbf{X}_i\boldsymbol{\beta}+\mathbf{Z}_i\mathbf{b}_i+\boldsymbol{\epsilon}_i$,
$i=1,\dots,m$.

-   $\boldsymbol{\beta}$: fixed effects ($p\times1$). $\mathbf{b}_i$:
    random effects ($q\times1$).
-   $\mathbf{b}_i\sim N(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{G})$,
    $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}_i\sim N(\mathbf{0},\sigma^2\mathbf{I})$,
    indep.
-   **Conditional mean:**
    $E(\mathbf{Y}_i|\mathbf{b}_i)=\mathbf{X}_i\boldsymbol{\beta}+\mathbf{Z}_i\mathbf{b}_i$.
-   **Marginal mean:** $E(\mathbf{Y}_i)=\mathbf{X}_i\boldsymbol{\beta}$
    (population).
-   **Marginal Var:**
    $\text{Var}(\mathbf{Y}_i)=\mathbf{Z}_i\mathbf{G}\mathbf{Z}_i^T+\sigma^2\mathbf{I}$.

### Random Intercept Model

$Y_{ij}=\beta_0+\mathbf{X}_{ij}^T\boldsymbol{\beta}+b_i+\epsilon_{ij}$,
$b_i\sim N(0,\sigma_b^2)$.

-   $\text{Var}(Y_{ij})=\sigma_b^2+\sigma^2$.
-   $\text{Cov}(Y_{ij},Y_{ik})=\sigma_b^2$ (induces **compound
    symmetry**).
-   **ICC:** $\rho=\sigma_b^2/(\sigma_b^2+\sigma^2)$.

### Random Intercept and Slope Model

$$Y_{ij}=\beta_1+\beta_2 t_{ij}+b_{1i}+b_{2i}t_{ij}+\epsilon_{ij}$$
$\mathbf{b}_i=(b_{1i},b_{2i})^T\sim N(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{G})$,
$\mathbf{G}=\begin{pmatrix}g_{11}&g_{12}\\g_{12}&g_{22}\end{pmatrix}$.

-   $\text{Var}(Y_{ij})=g_{11}+2t_{ij}g_{12}+t_{ij}^2g_{22}+\sigma^2$
    (varies w/ time).
-   $\text{Cov}(Y_{ij},Y_{ik})=g_{11}+(t_{ij}+t_{ik})g_{12}+t_{ij}t_{ik}g_{22}$.

## GEE (Lecture 19)

**Marginal Model for non-Gaussian longitudinal:**
$$g(\mu_{ij})=\mathbf{X}_{ij}^T\boldsymbol{\beta},\;\;\text{Var}(Y_{ij})=\phi V(\mu_{ij}),\;\;\text{corr}(Y_{ij},Y_{ik})=\alpha_{jk}$$

**Interpretation:** $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ has **population-averaged**
meaning. e.g., logistic GEE: $\beta_j$ = log OR comparing **subgroups**
of population differing in $X_j$.

## GLMM (Lecture 20)

**Generalized Linear Mixed Model:** Conditional on $\mathbf{b}_i$:
$$Y_{ij}|\mathbf{b}_i\sim\text{EF},\quad g(E(Y_{ij}|\mathbf{b}_i))=\mathbf{X}_{ij}^T\boldsymbol{\beta}+\mathbf{Z}_{ij}^T\mathbf{b}_i$$
$\mathbf{b}_i\sim N(\mathbf{0},\mathbf{G})$.

**Examples:**

-   **Logistic GLMM (random intercept):**
    $$\text{logit}(E(Y_{ij}|b_i))=b_i+\beta_1+X_{ij}\beta_2,\;\; b_i\sim N(0,\sigma_b^2)$$
-   **Poisson GLMM (random int+slope):**
    $$\log E(Y_{ij}|\mathbf{b}_i)=(b_{1i}+\beta_1)+(b_{2i}+\beta_2)t_{ij}$$

### Marginal vs GLMM (KEY DIFFERENCE!)

$$E(\mathbf{Y}_i)=\int g^{-1}(\mathbf{X}_i\boldsymbol{\beta}+\mathbf{Z}_i\mathbf{b}_i)f(\mathbf{b}_i)d\mathbf{b}_i\neq g^{-1}(\mathbf{X}_i\boldsymbol{\beta}_*)$$

-   For **nonlinear** $g$ (logit/log), GLMM $\boldsymbol{\beta}\neq$
    Marginal $\boldsymbol{\beta}_*$.
-   For **linear** $g$ (Gaussian), they coincide.
-   **Marginal** $\beta$: population-averaged effect.
-   **GLMM** $\beta$: subject-specific (conditional on $\mathbf{b}_i$)
    effect — for **same subject**, log-OR per unit $X$ change.
-   $|\beta_{GLMM}|>|\beta_{Marginal}|$ usually for binary outcomes.

# IV. Survival Analysis (Lecture 21)

-   **CDF:** $F(t)=P(T\leq t)$.
-   **Survival:** $S(t)=P(T>t)=1-F(t)$. $S(0)=1$, $S(\infty)=0$,
    decreasing.
-   **Hazard rate:** $h(t)=\frac{f(t)}{S(t)}=-\frac{d\log S(t)}{dt}$
-   **Cumulative hazard:** $H(t)=\int_0^t h(\tau)d\tau$.

**Key relations:** $S(t)=\exp\{-H(t)\}$, $f(t)=h(t)S(t)$.

**Parametric distributions:**

-   **Exponential:** $f(t)=\lambda e^{-\lambda t}$,
    $S(t)=e^{-\lambda t}$, $h(t)=\lambda$ (constant!).
-   **Weibull:** $S(t)=e^{-\lambda t^\alpha}$,
    $h(t)=\lambda\alpha t^{\alpha-1}$,
    $f(t)=\lambda\alpha t^{\alpha-1}e^{-\lambda t^\alpha}$.
    -   $\alpha>1$: increasing hazard; $\alpha<1$: decreasing;
        $\alpha=1$: exponential.

## Kaplan-Meier Estimator (Nonparametric)

For ordered times $t_1<\dots<t_m$:
$$\hat{S}(t)=\prod_{i:t_i\leq t}\left(1-\frac{d_i}{n_i}\right)$$

-   $n_i$: \# at risk just **before** $t_i$. $d_i$: \# events at $t_i$.
    Censored at $t_i$ counted in $n_i$ but not $d_i$.
-   $\hat\lambda_i=d_i/n_i$ = conditional prob of death at $t_i$.

**Greenwood Formula (variance of KM):**
$$\widehat{\text{Var}}(\hat S(t))=\hat S(t)^2\sum_{i:t_i\leq t}\frac{d_i}{(n_i-d_i)n_i}$$
95% CI: $\hat S(t)\pm1.96\widehat{SE}$ (truncate to [0,1]). Better:
build CI for $\log S$ or $\log(-\log S)$ then transform.

**Cumulative hazard:**

-   KM-based: $\hat H(t)=-\log\hat S(t)$.
-   **Nelson-Aalen** (better): $\tilde H(t)=\sum_{t_i\leq t}d_i/n_i$
    with $\widehat{\text{Var}}(\tilde H)=\sum d_i/n_i^2$.
-   **Fleming-Harrington:** $\hat S(t)=\exp(-\tilde H(t))$.

# V. Survival Curves (Lecture 22)

**Complete data, fixed time:** $\chi^2$ or Fisher exact on 2×2 (failed
before $t$).

**Censored data, fixed time** $t$ (use KM at $t$):
$$T=\frac{\hat S_A(t)-\hat S_B(t)}{\widehat{SD}\{\hat S_A(t)-\hat S_B(t)\}}\sim N(0,1)$$
$$\widehat{Var}\{\hat S_A-\hat S_B\}=\widehat{Var}\hat S_A+\widehat{Var}\hat S_B$$

## Log-Rank Test (Overall Difference)

$H_0:S_A(t)=S_B(t)\;\forall t$ (equivalently $h_A=h_B$).

At each **uncensored** time $t_i$ (pooled): build 2×2 (A vs B, event vs
no event).

-   $d_{A,i}\sim\text{Hypergeometric}(n_i,m_{D,i},n_{A,i})$ under $H_0$.
-   $E(d_{A,i})=m_{D,i}n_{A,i}/n_i$.
-   $\text{Var}(d_{A,i})=\dfrac{n_{A,i}n_{B,i}m_{D,i}m_{\bar D,i}}{n_i^2(n_i-1)}$.

**Test Statistic:**
$$Z=\frac{\sum_i\{d_{A,i}-E(d_{A,i})\}}{\sqrt{\sum_i\text{Var}(d_{A,i})}}\sim N(0,1),\;\; Z^2\sim\chi^2_1$$

**Weighted Log-Rank:** $T=\sum w_i\{d_{A,i}-E(d_{A,i})\}$.

-   $w_i=1$: log-rank (most powerful when HR proportional/late).
-   $w_i=n_i$: **Gehan**. $w_i=\sqrt{n_i}$: **Tarone-Ware**.
    $w_i=\hat S(t_i)^\rho\{1-\hat S(t_i)\}^\gamma$:
    **Fleming-Harrington**.

# VI. Survival Regression (Lecture 23)

## (a) Accelerated Failure Time (AFT) — Parametric

$$\log T_i=\mathbf{X}_i^T\boldsymbol{\beta}+\epsilon_i,\;\; T_i=\exp(\mathbf{X}_i^T\boldsymbol{\beta})T_{0i}$$

-   $\epsilon_i$ has parametric distribution
    (Weibull/Exponential/Log-normal).
-   $\exp(\beta_j)$: **time accelerator**. With unit $\uparrow x_j$,
    expected event time is $\exp(\beta_j)\times$ original.

## (b) Cox Proportional Hazards (PH) — Semiparametric

$$h_i(t)=h_0(t)\exp(\mathbf{X}_i^T\boldsymbol{\beta})$$

-   $h_0(t)$: **baseline hazard**, unspecified (nonparametric).
-   $\exp(\boldsymbol{\beta})$: **hazard ratio** (parametric).
-   **NO intercept** in $\mathbf{X}^T\boldsymbol{\beta}$ (absorbed in
    $h_0$).
-   Hazard **ratio**
    $h_i(t)/h_k(t)=\exp((\mathbf{X}_i-\mathbf{X}_k)^T\boldsymbol{\beta})$
    — **constant over** $t$.
-   $\beta_j$: log HR per unit $\uparrow x_j$.

## (c) Time-Dependent Covariates

$h_i(t)=h_0(t)\exp(\mathbf{x}_i(t)^T\boldsymbol{\beta})$. Use partial
likelihood with $\mathbf{x}_j$ replaced by $\mathbf{x}_j(t_{(i')})$ in
risk set. $\beta_j$: log HR per unit change at a given time.

## (d) Stratified PH Model

PH may not hold across all covariates. If a stratification covariate $S$
violates PH:
$$h_{is}(t)=h_{0s}(t)\exp(\mathbf{x}_i^T\boldsymbol{\beta})$$

-   Different baseline hazard per stratum, **same** $\boldsymbol{\beta}$
    (HR constant **within** strata).
